All Collections Customizing Transcripts and Captions Transcripts and Captions Increase your content's accessibility and optimize your videos for SEO with captions and transcripts. Written by Katie October 14, 2026 Table of contents Not only are transcripts and captions critical for accessibility, but they also help make long-form content more digestible for your audience and contribute to SEO optimization. Captions vs. transcripts Captions and transcripts go hand-in-hand in Wistia, but there are fundamental differences between them: Captions display all audible dialogue in real time and are only available in the video player. Captions are enabled from the play bar. Transcripts are time-coded logs of all dialogue in a media and are available for both video and audio files. Transcripts can be found below the player on media pages or in Channels. Captions and transcripts are connected in Wistia; changes made to a transcript will be applied to the corresponding captions and vice versa. Note Editing a transcript will not update burnt-in captions that have already been saved to a video. Order captions and transcripts All current Wistia plans include free computer-generated transcripts and captions. To order a new transcript, click "Generate transcript" on the media page. In the order modal, you'll be prompted to select the transcript type and language. Tip Select the "Automatically enable captions when they're ready" option before ordering to ensure that your captions are available on your video as soon as possible. If you’d prefer to review the captions before they go live, you can uncheck this option before ordering. Transcript prices and turnaround times vary based on your selection: Transcript type Details Pricing Turnaround Automated Computer-generated, 95% accuracy Free Within minutes Professional Human-reviewed, 99% accuracy 1,000 credits per minute Within 4 business days Professional (rush order) Human-reviewed, 99% accuracy 1,600 credits per minute Within one business day Automatic transcript ordering Transcripts cannot be applied to multiple existing videos in bulk. However, you can enable automatic transcript ordering for future uploads in your account settings . This setting applies only to videos uploaded after you turn it on, not to your existing library. Tip If you have developer resources or experience, you can order transcripts programmatically using our Captions API . Smart formatting Automated transcripts use smart formatting, so spoken numbers, dates, times, currency, phone numbers, email addresses, and URLs come back written the way you'd type them rather than spelled out. For example, you'll see "2026" instead of "twenty twenty-six," "10:59 AM" instead of "ten fifty-nine AM," and "$1.5 million" instead of "one point five million dollars." This carries through to your captions, chapters, and Remix edits automatically, so you have less to fix by hand. Note Smart formatting applies to newly generated transcripts after September 15, 2026. You can delete previously ordered transcripts and regenerate them to apply smart formatting. Upload captions If you have an existing SRT or VTT file for your video, open the ellipsis menu and select "Upload". You can upload as many caption files as you'd like. Note While we accept WebVTT files, they will be converted to SRT format upon upload. Thus, we cannot support any styling or positioning instructions. From here, drag and drop files or click "Select files." We'll automatically detect the language and notify you of any formatting errors upon uploading. Once uploaded and validated, click "Save." Tip If you’re using a language that reads right-to-left, you’ll need to accommodate the flip that occurs in many internet environments. Wistia flips right-to-left transcripts by default, so we recommend building captions to account for this. If you're having trouble uploading a custom captions file, check out our troubleshooting guide for failed captions uploads . Keywords glossary If certain words in your media might be more difficult to transcribe (e.g., acronyms, industry terms, product names), you can add a list of keywords to your account. Scroll down to the "Keywords glossary" section of your Account Settings page to add known terms for computer-generated transcripts. Once complete, click "Save Changes." Note The Keywords glossary can support up to 100 words. Enable captions by default Once you've added a transcript to your video, you'll have the option to enable captions by default for your viewers. On your media page, click "Customize," then open the Controls tab. Here, select your default captions behavior. If enabled by default, captions will be visible on the screen for all viewers. If set to off by default, viewers must enable captions manually via the CC button in the play bar. Edit a transcript In the transcript section of your media page, click "Edit" to correct any spelling or transcript errors. Click "Save" to apply your changes to the transcript and captions. Open the ellipsis menu to access multiple options for your transcripts and captions. Upload an SRT or VTT file Order a professional transcript Delete a transcript Download a transcript Copy the transcript text Generate chapters from the transcript Correct captions timing Hide speakers from viewers Correct captions timing Need to adjust the timing of words or phrases in your captions? Click on the ellipsis menu and select "Correct captions timing" to open the editor. If you have transcript files in multiple languages, you can select which one you’d like to edit. Click into the dropdown menu to select your desired language. From here, you can move words around your timeline as necessary, extend how long they’ll display, and customize any line breaks in the text. Select a specific word to adjust it, or click the point in the timeline you want to change. The bars above each group of text can be used to control: How long a block of text appears on the video How long a break between captions is How many words appear in a block of text You can drag the carriage return icon to determine where line breaks should appear. If you make any mistakes, click "Undo" or "Redo." To remove a line break, select it and click "Delete." Click the keyboard to view keyboard shortcuts. To exit the captions editor without making changes, click "Cancel." If you’re ready to save your changes, click "Save." Viewer caption settings Viewers can customize caption settings to their preference from the play bar. To customize caption settings, click into the captions menu from the play bar and select "Captions settings." Here, you can adjust several settings for how your captions appear in your video. The following settings can be customized: Font size Font family Font color Font opacity Character edge style Background color Background opacity Window color Window opacity Selected settings will be saved automatically for that browser session. If you change your mind, scroll down to the bottom of the modal and click "Reset to defaults." Browser language detection If you’re working with multilingual captions, we’ll supply the captions that match the language of your viewer’s browser. If those captions aren’t available, we’ll serve English captions by default. When viewers enable captions and select a language on a video, their selections will be saved for all future viewing sessions on the same domain. With these preferences saved, viewers will only need to enable captions once in a learning course, video series, or a Wistia Channel. Caption settings will not persist across other browsers or devices. Interactive transcripts Interactive transcripts allow viewers to navigate to different parts of your media by scrolling through or searching the captions file. Open the captions menu from the play bar and select “Search Video" to search for keywords or phrases. A search bar will appear in the player. Below the media, the transcript will also highlight each word as it is spoken. Click on any word to navigate to that point in the media. Translate transcripts To create a new translation of your transcript, click the language dropdown menu and select "Manage localizations." From here, select "Text translation." Search for or select your desired language from the dropdown menu and click "Order." You can then select which language you’d like to view as captions in your video by clicking the captions icon on the play bar. Download videos with captions When downloading a video on the media page, you'll see a checkbox to "Include available captions" for any existing transcripts. Check this option to download an asset with captions. Uncompressed media files cannot be downloaded with captions. Note Captions cannot be downloaded with a dubbed version of a video. Open the downloaded file in your media player of choice and select the captions track you'd like to display. Tip Some media players (like Windows Media Player) may not support captions included with a video. If you run into this issue, you can try downloading the caption file separately and then manually adding it to the video. Download transcript To download a transcript in SRT format, open the ellipsis menu and click "Download". The transcript will be downloaded in SRT format. To download the transcript in a different format, open the ellipsis menu next to the "Embed" button. In the Download modal, click the "Transcript" tab, then select your desired language and format (SRT, VTT, or TXT). You may also copy the transcript text to your clipboard by clicking the icon to the left of the "Download" button. The language and format you have selected will be copied. Multiple transcript languages must be downloaded separately. Delete transcript and captions When you delete a video's translation, both the transcript and captions in that language will be removed. In order to do so, in the dropdown menu of the Transcript section, select "Manage localizations." In the "Manage localizations" modal, click the ellipsis menu, then select "Delete." Confirm your decision in the pop-up window. Once done, that language will be removed from your video. Note Deleted transcripts cannot be recovered. If you delete a dubbed translation that you have purchased, or human-generated captions, and change your mind, you will need to repurchase the language. Automatic player translations Player controls will be translated automatically based on the viewer's caption or dub language selection. For example, if you enable French captions in the player, all text in the player, including speed and quality controls, Chapters, Wistia Forms, etc., will also be translated to French. If player translations are not available for a specific caption language, we'll default to English. Transcript search Note Transcript search is currently in beta. When you search for content in your account, this will surface any related transcripts. You can also filter search results to include only transcripts. In the search modal, click “Transcript Only - Beta.” Your search results will be limited to transcript content only. Click "Transcript only - Beta" again to expand search results to titles, descriptions, tags, and more. Read Dell’s Story Connect with our Team to Get Started Sign Up Here Loading form… Captioning FAQs What is closed captioning? Closed captioning is the time-synchronized, textual display of a video’s dialogue and all essential non-speech audio (like music or sound effects) that viewers can turn on or off, making video content fully accessible to the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. You can learn more in our article, The Ultimate Guide to Closed Captioning . Do you offer live captions? Yes, we offer both live professional captioning and live automatic captioning powered by automated speech recognition. Our live captioning services integrate seamlessly with platforms like YouTube, Zoom, Facebook, Brightcove, JW Player, and any RTMP stream. What captioning languages do you offer? We support captioning in 50+ languages, including Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, and many more. View the full list of supported languages. What is Predicted Caption Accuracy? Predicted Caption Accuracy is a proprietary feature from 3Play Media that uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) to estimate the quality and Word Error Rate (WER) of a machine-generated caption file before a human has reviewed it. This allows you to set accuracy thresholds to either post back ASR or automatically upgrade to human review. Do you offer caption placement? We offer automated and manual caption placement services to help you meet FCC requirements cost-effectively. Automated caption placement uses an algorithm to analyze the screen and determine the position of the caption frame. With manual caption placement, a transcript editor personally checks the placement of each caption frame, ensuring 100% that captions don’t block important visual elements. Do you offer automated speech recognition/auto captions? Yes, we offer Automated Speech Recognition (ASR) , or auto captions, with an option to add human review at a later time Click here to learn more about ASR. What is your accuracy for captioning/transcription? We guarantee a minimum of 99% accuracy and our actual measured accuracy averages 99.6%. We achieve this level of accuracy the first time and every time, eliminating the need for review and rework. This article describes the effort we invest to make sure we always achieve at least 99% accuracy. Do you split media files among numerous transcriptionists? No. Many vendors chop up each video into micro segments that are split up among numerous transcriptionists. This creates inconsistencies and quality issues. We use a single transcriptionist to work on a file from beginning to end. This ensures that the transcriptionist has the full context of the content to better identify proper nouns and that the transcript contains completely consistent standards and spellings. What differentiates 3Play Media’s transcriptionists? Our transcriptionists are a critical part of our process at 3Play Media, and are treated as such. All transcriptionists go through a rigorous certification process. They are unique individuals who are detail-oriented, have a strong grasp of English grammar, and are eager to help your content be the best and most accessible it can be. What if I need a truly flawless transcript? If you need a flawless transcript, we offer a full review option. This typically increases accuracy to 99.9%. Another option is to review and edit the files yourself, using the caption editor. Contact Us Ready to scale video without the risk? Let’s talk. Most website accessibility audits range between $1,250 and $2,750. Pricing is $100 to $250 per primary page or screen and $25 to $100 for light pages or screens. Because our audits are custom and fully manual, your final cost depends on scope, status, and complexity. How is the audit price determined? Three factors set the price: scope (the number and type of pages or screens in your representative sample), status (how accessible the asset already is), and complexity (interactive components, dynamic content, and custom widgets). We evaluate a representative sample rather than every page. What is the difference between a primary page and a light page? Primary pages are content rich or interactive pages and screens, priced at $100 to $250 each. Light pages have minimal content or repeated patterns and are priced lower, at $25 to $100 each. We complete the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT) and produce a finished Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR) based on the audit. Other editions are Section 508 at $550, EN 301 549 at $650, and the INT combined edition at $950. The different amounts represent the time necessary to fill out the different editions. What WCAG standards do you evaluate against? We evaluate digital assets against WCAG 2.1 AA or WCAG 2.2 AA, and occasionally WCAG 2.0 AA. Are your audits manual or automated? Fully manual. There is no such thing as an automated audit. Our technical accessibility experts will evaluate your asset using screen reader testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, and/or TalkBack), keyboard testing, visual inspection, and code inspection. We use an automated scan only as a review, to confirm that every scan detectable issue is included in the final audit report. What do I receive at the end of an audit?
